question: Which of the following shortcut key is used to repeat the last command or action, if possible, in MS-Excel 365?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ctrl + Y.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In MS-Excel 365 (and other MS Office applications), Ctrl + Y is the Repeat shortcut — it repeats the last command or action performed, if it is possible to repeat it. (पुनः दोहराना)

 

• The F4 key also performs the same “Repeat” function in Excel.

 

• Ctrl + Z is used for Undo, which reverses the last action — it is the opposite of Repeat/Redo.

 

• The Repeat command is context-sensitive: it repeats whatever the last action was, such as applying formatting, inserting a row, or typing text.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ctrl + C, Ctrl + X, and Ctrl + V are used for Copy, Cut, and Paste respectively.

 

• Ctrl + S saves the current workbook, and Ctrl + P opens the print dialog.

 

NOTE

 

• Ctrl + Z (Option 1): This is the shortcut for Undo, which reverses the previous action rather than repeating it.

 

• Shift + Z (Option 2): This is not a standard, defined shortcut in MS-Excel 365 for repeat or redo.

 

• Shift + Y (Option 4): This is not a standard, defined shortcut in MS-Excel 365 for repeat or redo.

question: Who built the Pathar Ki Masjid in Patna, Bihar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Parwez Shah.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pathar Ki Masjid (Stone Mosque) in Patna, Bihar, was built in 1626 CE by Sultan Parwez Shah (Prince Parvez), the eldest son of the Mughal emperor Jahangir, when he was the Subedar (governor) of Bihar. (पत्थर की मस्जिद — पटना)

 

• The mosque is built almost entirely of stone, which is unusual for the region and gives it its name.

 

• It is located on the banks of the river Ganga in Patna and is considered one of the oldest Mughal-era mosques in Bihar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable Mughal-era monuments in Patna include the area around the Khuda Baksh Oriental Library and the Sher Shah Suri Mosque (Afghan Masjid), built under the earlier Sur dynasty.

 

• Prince Parvez was known primarily as a Mughal prince and military commander, and this mosque stands as one of the few architectural monuments credited to him.

 

NOTE

 

• Feroz shah Tughlaq (Option 1): A 14th-century Delhi Sultanate ruler known for building cities like Firozabad and monuments such as Feroz Shah Kotla; unrelated to this mosque.

 

• Aurangzeb (Option 3): A later Mughal emperor known for structures like the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore; he did not build the Pathar Ki Masjid.

 

• Alauddin Khilji (Option 4): A Delhi Sultanate ruler of the Khilji dynasty, known for the Alai Darwaza and Siri Fort; unconnected to this Patna mosque.

question: If the price elasticity of demand is less than one, then the demand for the goods is said to be ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Inelastic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Price elasticity of demand (Ed) measures the responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price. When Ed < 1, demand is said to be inelastic — a given percentage change in price causes a smaller percentage change in quantity demanded. (लोचहीन मांग)

 

• When Ed = 0, demand is perfectly inelastic — quantity demanded does not change at all with price.

 

• When Ed = ∞, demand is perfectly elastic — even a negligible price change causes an infinite change in quantity demanded.

 

• When Ed = 1, demand is unitary elastic — the percentage change in quantity demanded equals the percentage change in price.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Goods with few substitutes and necessities (like salt, medicines) generally have inelastic demand.

 

• When Ed > 1, demand is called elastic demand.

 

NOTE

 

• Perfectly inelastic (Option 1): This corresponds to Ed = 0, not Ed < 1.

 

• Perfectly elastic (Option 3): This corresponds to Ed = ∞, an extreme case, not Ed < 1.

 

• Unitary-elastic (Option 4): This corresponds to Ed = 1 exactly, not Ed < 1.

question: Rishu wants to input data to the computer by pressing keys. Which input device should he use?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Keyboard.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A keyboard is an input device that allows a user to enter data into a computer by pressing keys representing letters, numbers, symbols, and control functions. (कुंजीपटल — कुंजी दबाकर डेटा इनपुट)

 

• It is the most common and primary text/data-entry device used with computers.

 

• Standard keyboards (like the QWERTY layout) contain alphanumeric keys, function keys, and special keys such as Enter, Shift, and Ctrl.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other common input devices include the mouse, microphone, and webcam, but they are not used for entering data by pressing keys.

 

• Keyboards can be wired or wireless and connect to a computer via USB, PS/2, or Bluetooth.

 

NOTE

 

• Scanner (Option 2): An input device used to convert physical documents or images into digital form; it does not involve pressing keys to input data.

 

• Joystick (Option 3): An input device mainly used for controlling movement in games and simulations, not for typing data.

 

• Light Pen (Option 4): A pointing device used to select or draw directly on a display screen, not for entering data via keys.

question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Industrial Policy resolution 1956?
I. This resolution formed the basis of the Second Five Year Plan.
II. This policy was used for promoting industry in backward regions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR), 1956 was adopted by the Government of India and is regarded as the “Economic Constitution of India”; it classified industries into three categories (Schedule A, B, and C) based on the role of the state. (औद्योगिक नीति संकल्प, 1956)

 

• Statement I is correct: The IPR 1956 provided the basic framework for India's industrial policy and directly formed the basis for the Second Five Year Plan (1956–61), which emphasised rapid industrialisation with a focus on heavy and basic industries.

 

• Statement II is correct: The resolution also aimed at reducing regional disparities by promoting the establishment of industries in backward and underdeveloped regions of the country.

 

• Since both statements accurately describe the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956, the correct choice is “Both I and II”.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The IPR 1956 gave the public sector a dominant role in the economy and reserved key industries such as railways, atomic energy, and iron and steel for the state.

 

• It was preceded by the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948 and later modified by subsequent policies, notably the New Industrial Policy of 1991.

 

NOTE

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 1): Incorrect, since both statements are factually accurate descriptions of the IPR 1956.

 

• Only I (Option 3): Incomplete, since Statement II regarding promotion of industry in backward regions is also correct.

 

• Only II (Option 4): Incomplete, since Statement I regarding the basis of the Second Five Year Plan is also correct.

question: Which of the following seasons in India is known as the transition season?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Retreating Monsoon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Retreating (or Post/South-West) Monsoon season, spanning October–November, is known as the transition season in India because it marks the changeover from the hot, humid rainy season to the dry, cool winter season. (मानसून वापसी — संक्रमण काल)

 

• During this period, the monsoon trough weakens and withdraws from north-west India towards the Bay of Bengal, causing a distinct rise in day temperature along with a fall in night temperature, and clear skies.

 

• This season is also associated with the formation of cyclones on the eastern coast of India (Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha) due to the retreating monsoon picking up moisture over the Bay of Bengal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's climatic year is broadly divided into four seasons: Cold Weather Season (winter), Hot Weather Season (summer), Advancing/South-West Monsoon Season (rainy), and Retreating Monsoon Season (transition/autumn).

 

• The Tamil Nadu coast receives most of its rainfall during the retreating monsoon (October–December) via the north-east monsoon winds.

 

NOTE

 

• Advancing Monsoon (Option 2): This refers to the South-West Monsoon (June–September), the main rainy season, not the transition period.

 

• Cold Weather Season (Option 3): This is the winter season (December–February), following the transition period, not the transition itself.

 

• Hot Weather Season (Option 4): This is the summer season (March–May), preceding the monsoon, not a transition season.

question: ‘2G Saga Unfolds’ book was written by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andimuthu Raja.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• ‘2G Saga Unfolds’ is a book written by former Union Telecom Minister Andimuthu (A.) Raja, in which he gave his account of the 2G spectrum allocation case. (2जी घोटाला — ए. राजा की पुस्तक)

 

• The book was published in 2016 and presents Raja's defence and version of events surrounding the allotment of 2G telecom licences during his tenure as Communications Minister (2007–2009).

 

• A. Raja was later acquitted, along with other co-accused, by a special CBI court in the 2G spectrum case in December 2017.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• A. Raja was a member of the DMK party and represented the Nilgiris constituency in Tamil Nadu in the Lok Sabha.

 

• The 2G spectrum case was one of the biggest corruption controversies in independent India, alleging a loss to the exchequer in the allocation of telecom licences in 2008.

 

NOTE

 

• Mohsin Hamid (Option 1): A Pakistani novelist known for works such as ‘The Reluctant Fundamentalist’ and ‘Exit West’, unrelated to this book.

 

• Tarun Vijay (Option 2): A former BJP Rajya Sabha member and author/columnist, but not the author of ‘2G Saga Unfolds’.

 

• Kanwaljit Singh (Option 4): Not connected to the authorship of this book on the 2G spectrum case.

question: At places the groundwater is stored between layers of hard rock below the water table. This is known as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is an aquifer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An aquifer is an underground layer of permeable rock, gravel, sand, or silt that stores and yields groundwater; it lies below the water table and is often sandwiched between layers of impermeable (hard) rock. (जलभृत — भूजल का भंडारण)

 

• Water percolates through soil and porous rock and gets stored in the aquifer, from where it can be extracted through wells or tube-wells, or may naturally emerge as springs.

 

• Aquifers are broadly classified as confined (trapped between impermeable layers) and unconfined (with the water table as the upper boundary).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The zone of saturation, where all pore spaces are filled with water, lies below the water table and is part of the aquifer system.

 

• Over-extraction of groundwater from aquifers leads to a fall in the water table, causing water scarcity — a major concern in many parts of India.

 

NOTE

 

• a well (Option 1): A well is a man-made structure dug or drilled to access and extract groundwater from an aquifer; it is not the storage layer itself.

 

• a lake (Option 3): A lake is a surface water body, not a layer of rock storing groundwater underground.

 

• a pond (Option 4): A pond is also a small surface water body, unrelated to underground rock layers storing water.

question: In humans, the digestion of carbohydrates like starch, begins in which of the following parts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Buccal cavity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The digestion of carbohydrates like starch begins in the buccal cavity (mouth), where the enzyme salivary amylase (ptyalin), secreted by the salivary glands, breaks down starch into simpler sugars like maltose. (मुख गुहा — लार एमाइलेज)

 

• Mechanical digestion also begins here, as chewing (mastication) breaks food into smaller pieces and mixes it with saliva to form a bolus.

 

• Salivary amylase works best in a slightly alkaline/neutral pH and stops acting once food reaches the highly acidic environment of the stomach.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Protein digestion begins in the stomach with the enzyme pepsin, while fat digestion mainly occurs in the small intestine with the help of bile and lipase.

 

• Most of the carbohydrate digestion is completed in the small intestine by enzymes like pancreatic amylase and intestinal maltase, sucrase, and lactase.

 

NOTE

 

• Rectum (Option 1): The rectum is the final part of the large intestine involved in storing and eliminating waste, not in the initiation of digestion.

 

• Small Intestine (Option 2): Carbohydrate digestion continues and is completed here, but it does not begin here.

 

• Oesophagus (Option 3): The oesophagus is merely a passage that transports food from the mouth to the stomach via peristalsis; no digestion occurs here.

question: ______ is a tributary of river Godavari.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indravati.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indravati River is a major left-bank tributary of the river Godavari; it originates in the Eastern Ghats of Odisha and flows through Chhattisgarh before joining the Godavari near the Chhattisgarh–Andhra Pradesh–Telangana border. (इंद्रावती नदी — गोदावरी की सहायक नदी)

 

• Other important tributaries of the Godavari include the Pranhita, Manjira, Penganga, Wardha, and Sabari.

 

• The Godavari is the largest river of peninsular India and is often called the “Dakshin Ganga” (Ganga of the South).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indravati Tiger Reserve in Chhattisgarh is named after this river.

 

• The Godavari originates near Trimbakeshwar in the Nashik district of Maharashtra and drains into the Bay of Bengal.

 

NOTE

 

• Tawa (Option 1): The Tawa is a tributary of the river Narmada, not the Godavari.

 

• Banas (Option 2): The Banas (in Rajasthan) is a tributary of the Chambal river; there is also a separate Banas river in Gujarat that drains into the Rann of Kutch — neither joins the Godavari.

 

• Chambal (Option 4): The Chambal is a major tributary of the river Yamuna, not the Godavari.

question: Which union territory of India has a sea named after it?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Andaman Sea, a marginal sea of the Bay of Bengal, is named after the union territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands, which lies within it. (अंडमान सागर)

 

• The Andaman Sea lies between the Andaman and Nicobar Islands to the west and Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia, and Sumatra (Indonesia) to the east and south.

 

• Andaman and Nicobar Islands is a union territory of India with its capital at Port Blair, comprising over 570 islands.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ten Degree Channel separates the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands.

 

• India's union territories include Puducherry, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Chandigarh, Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh.

 

NOTE

 

• Puducherry (Option 1): No sea is named after this union territory; it lies along the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea coasts of India.

 

• Dadra and Nagar Haveli (Option 3): This is a landlocked union territory located on India's west coast region, with no sea named after it.

 

• Daman and Diu (Option 4): This union territory lies on the coast of the Arabian Sea but does not have a sea named after it.

question: Who emphasized the worship of God as Nirankar (Formless) in Punjab?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Baba Dayal Das.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Baba Dayal Das founded the Nirankari movement in Punjab in the early 19th century, emphasising the worship of God as Nirankar, meaning “formless” or “without shape.” (निरंकारी आंदोलन — बाबा दयाल दास)

 

• The movement stressed a return to the pure, monotheistic teachings of Guru Nanak and opposed idol worship and ritualism that had crept into Sikh religious practice.

 

• It was one of several 19th-century reform movements among the Sikhs, alongside movements like the Namdhari (Kuka) movement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Namdhari (Kuka) movement, which emphasised social reform and cow protection, was led by Baba Ram Singh.

 

• Maharaja Ranjit Singh was the founder of the Sikh Empire in Punjab, known for his political and military achievements, not for a religious reform movement.

 

NOTE

 

• Maharaja Ranjit Singh (Option 1): He was the founder and ruler of the Sikh Empire, focused on political consolidation of Punjab, not a religious reformer of the Nirankari type.

 

• Baba Ram Singh (Option 2): He founded the Namdhari (Kuka) movement, a separate 19th-century Sikh reform movement, not the Nirankari movement.

 

• Guru Gobind Singh (Option 4): He was the tenth Sikh Guru, who founded the Khalsa Panth in 1699; he lived earlier and is not associated with founding the 19th-century Nirankari movement.

question:
Which of the following pair of "term – sport" is NOT correct?
I. Batting – Cricket
II. Goal – Netball
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neither I nor II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I (Batting – Cricket) is a correct pairing: “Batting” is a fundamental term used in cricket, referring to the act of facing bowling and scoring runs with a bat. (क्रिकेट — बल्लेबाजी)

 

• Statement II (Goal – Netball) is also a correct pairing: In netball, points are scored by shooting the ball through a hoop, and each successful shot is called a “goal”, similar to terminology used in football and hockey.

 

• Since both pairings correctly match the term with its associated sport, neither pair I nor pair II is incorrect.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Netball is a team sport, derived from early forms of basketball, played mainly by women, with seven players per side.

 

• Common cricket terms include “wicket,” “over,” “innings,” and “boundary,” alongside “batting” and “bowling.”

 

NOTE

 

• Both I and II (Option 1): Incorrect, as both pairs I and II correctly match the term to its sport.

 

• Only I (Option 2): Incorrect, since pair I (Batting – Cricket) is a correct pairing, not an incorrect one.

 

• Only II (Option 3): Incorrect, since pair II (Goal – Netball) is also a correct pairing, not an incorrect one.

question: Concurrent list of seventh schedule does NOT have provision related to ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Taxes on lands and buildings.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Concurrent List (List III) of the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains subjects on which both the Union and State governments can legislate; it includes entries such as “Trade unions; industrial and labour disputes” (Entry 22), “Forests” (Entry 17A), and “Economic and social planning” (Entry 20). (समवर्ती सूची — सातवीं अनुसूची)

 

• “Taxes on lands and buildings” is Entry 49 of the State List (List II), not the Concurrent List — it falls exclusively within the legislative domain of the State Legislatures.

 

• Since it is a State List subject, “Taxes on lands and buildings” is the one option among those given that is NOT a Concurrent List provision.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Concurrent List originally had 47 entries (as per the original Constitution) and now has 52 entries after subsequent amendments, including the 42nd Amendment (1976), which moved subjects like “Forests” and “Education” from the State List to the Concurrent List.

 

• In case of a conflict between a Union law and a State law on a Concurrent List subject, the Union law prevails, as per Article 254.

 

NOTE

 

• Industrial and labour disputes (Option 1): This is Entry 22 of the Concurrent List, so it IS a Concurrent List subject.

 

• Forests (Option 2): This is Entry 17A of the Concurrent List (moved here by the 42nd Amendment), so it IS a Concurrent List subject.

 

• Economic and social planning (Option 4): This is Entry 20 of the Concurrent List, so it IS a Concurrent List subject.

question: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the United Nations World Geospatial Congress (UNWGIC) 2022 held in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hyderabad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the second United Nations World Geospatial Information Congress (UNWGIC) 2022 at the Hyderabad International Convention Centre (HICC), Hyderabad, on 11 October 2022. (संयुक्त राष्ट्र विश्व भू-स्थानिक कांग्रेस — हैदराबाद)

 

• The theme of UNWGIC 2022 was “Geo-enabling the Global Village: No one should be left behind.”

 

• The congress was jointly organised by the UN Committee of Experts on Global Geospatial Information Management (UN-GGIM) and the Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first edition of UNWGIC was held in Deqing, China, in 2018.

 

• At the event, PM Modi also released a stamp and coin to commemorate the occasion and highlighted India's liberalised Geospatial Data Policy of 2021.

 

NOTE

 

• Bangalore (Option 1): UNWGIC 2022 was not held here, although Bengaluru is a major hub for India's space and technology sectors.

 

• Mumbai (Option 2): UNWGIC 2022 was not held in Mumbai.

 

• Pune (Option 4): UNWGIC 2022 was not held in Pune.

question: Suresh N Patel was appointed as chief of which organization in August 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Central Vigilance Commission.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Suresh N. Patel, a former Chairman and Managing Director of Andhra Bank, was appointed as the Central Vigilance Commissioner (CVC) of India in August 2022. (केंद्रीय सतर्कता आयुक्त)

 

• He was appointed by a committee comprising the Prime Minister, the Home Minister, and the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, as per the CVC appointment process.

 

• The Central Vigilance Commission is the apex Indian governmental body created to address governmental corruption, established in 1964 and given statutory status under the CVC Act, 2003.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Central Vigilance Commission is headquartered in New Delhi and functions as an autonomous body, free of control from any executive authority.

 

• The CVC was set up on the recommendation of the Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption (1962–64).

 

NOTE

 

• NITI Ayog (Option 1): NITI Aayog is India's premier policy think tank, chaired by the Prime Minister and headed by a Vice-Chairperson; Suresh N. Patel was not appointed here.

 

• SEBI (Option 2): The Securities and Exchange Board of India was chaired by Madhabi Puri Buch as of 2022, not Suresh N. Patel.

 

• Election Commission of India (Option 3): The Chief Election Commissioner in 2022 was Rajiv Kumar, not Suresh N. Patel.

question: In May 2022, RailTel launched PM-WANI based on ______.
option_4: access to its Wi-Fi at 100 railway stations
solution_text:
The correct answer is access to its Wi-Fi at 100 railway stations.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In May 2022, RailTel (a Miniratna PSU under the Ministry of Railways) launched a service under the PM-WANI (Prime Minister Wi-Fi Access Network Interface) scheme, providing public access to its Wi-Fi hotspots at 100 railway stations across the country. (पीएम-वाणी — मुफ्त सार्वजनिक वाई-फाई)

 

• PM-WANI is a government initiative launched in December 2020 to proliferate public Wi-Fi networks across the country through Public Data Offices (PDOs), without requiring licence fees.

 

• RailTel already provides free Wi-Fi services at over 6,100 railway stations under its RailWire brand; the PM-WANI initiative expanded interoperable public Wi-Fi access under a unified framework.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• PM-WANI aims to boost Digital India by enabling small shopkeepers and local entrepreneurs to set up public Wi-Fi hotspots as Public Data Office Aggregators (PDOAs).

 

• RailTel Corporation of India is also known for laying an extensive optic fibre network along railway tracks across India.

 

NOTE

 

• food subsidy in 100 trains (Option 1): RailTel's PM-WANI initiative concerned Wi-Fi access, not any food subsidy scheme.

 

• fire safety scheme (Option 2): This is unrelated to the PM-WANI-based initiative launched by RailTel in May 2022.

 

• free travel insurance scheme (Option 3): This is unrelated to the PM-WANI Wi-Fi initiative; travel insurance is a separate railway ticketing feature.

question: In Kheda, Gujarat, Patidar peasants organised non-violent campaigns against which of the following demand of the British?
solution_text:
The correct answer is High land revenue.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kheda Satyagraha (1918) was a non-violent protest launched by peasants, largely Patidars, in the Kheda district of Gujarat, against the British government's demand for full land revenue payment despite crop failure caused by drought and famine conditions. (खेडा सत्याग्रह — 1918)

 

• Under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi, along with Vallabhbhai Patel and Indulal Yagnik, the peasants demanded remission/suspension of land revenue, since the crop yield had fallen below the level exempting them from tax under existing rules.

 

• The satyagraha ended with the government agreeing to suspend revenue collection for the poorer cultivators until conditions improved.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• This was one of Gandhi's earliest satyagrahas in India after his return from South Africa, following the Champaran Satyagraha (1917) in Bihar over indigo cultivation.

 

• Vallabhbhai Patel earned significant recognition and leadership standing in Gujarat through his role in the Kheda Satyagraha.

 

NOTE

 

• Low labour rates (Option 1): This was not the issue in the Kheda Satyagraha, which concerned agricultural land revenue, not industrial wage rates.

 

• Long working hours (Option 2): This is unrelated; it typically pertains to labour/factory movements, not the Kheda peasant movement.

 

• Low price for crops (Option 4): The core grievance was the demand for high land revenue despite crop failure, not merely low crop prices.

question: Which article of the Indian constitution specifies the composition of the Council of States?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 80.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 80 of the Indian Constitution deals with the composition of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha), providing for a maximum of 250 members — up to 12 nominated by the President for their special knowledge in fields like literature, science, art, and social service, and the rest elected by the Legislative Assemblies of the States and Union Territories. (राज्यसभा की संरचना — अनुच्छेद 80)

 

• Rajya Sabha members representing States are elected through indirect election by the method of proportional representation using single transferable votes.

 

• Article 80 falls under Part V of the Constitution, which deals with the Union government.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The composition of the House of the People (Lok Sabha) is dealt with under Article 81.

 

• The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body, not subject to dissolution, with one-third of its members retiring every two years.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 395 (Option 2): This is the final article of the Constitution, dealing with repeals of the Indian Independence Act, 1947, and the Government of India Act, 1935.

 

• Article 51A (Option 3): This article lists the Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens, added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment, 1976.

 

• Article 12 (Option 4): This article defines the term “State” for the purposes of Part III (Fundamental Rights) of the Constitution.

question: Which city will host the 2032 Summer Olympic Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brisbane.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Brisbane, Australia, was selected to host the 2032 Summer Olympic Games — this will be the third time Australia hosts the Olympics, after Melbourne (1956) and Sydney (2000). (2032 ओलंपिक — ब्रिसबेन, ऑस्ट्रेलिया)

 

• The International Olympic Committee (IOC) confirmed Brisbane as host at its 138th session in Tokyo on 21 July 2021, adopting a new, more flexible targeted-dialogue bid process rather than a traditional multi-city bidding contest.

 

• Brisbane will host the games alongside co-host cities within the state of Queensland, and it will also host the 2032 Paralympic Games.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2024 Summer Olympics were held in Paris, France, and the 2028 Summer Olympics are scheduled for Los Angeles, USA.

 

• Tokyo hosted the 2020 Summer Olympics (held in 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic).

 

NOTE

 

• Athens (Option 1): Athens hosted the first modern Olympic Games in 1896, and again in 2004; it is not the host for 2032.

 

• Jakarta (Option 2): Jakarta, Indonesia, has hosted the Asian Games but is not the host city for the 2032 Summer Olympics.

 

• Tokyo (Option 4): Tokyo hosted the 2020 Summer Olympics (held in 2021), not the 2032 edition.

question: The Natya shastra which provides information regarding musical instruments is compiled by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharat Muni.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Natya Shastra, an ancient Sanskrit treatise on the performing arts encompassing dance, drama, and music, was compiled by Bharata Muni, believed to date back to between 200 BCE and 200 CE. (नाट्यशास्त्र — भरत मुनि)

 

• It provides detailed information on musical instruments (Vadya), classifying them into four categories: Tata (stringed), Avanaddha (percussion/membranophones), Ghana (solid/idiophones), and Sushira (wind).

 

• The Natya Shastra also laid the theoretical foundation for classical Indian dance forms, dramaturgy, aesthetics (rasa theory), and music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bharata Muni is often referred to as the “father of Indian theatrical art” for his contributions through the Natya Shastra.

 

• The rasa theory (theory of aesthetic emotions), a cornerstone of Indian classical arts and literature, was first elaborated in the Natya Shastra.

 

NOTE

 

• Amir Khusrau (Option 1): A 13th–14th century poet, musician, and scholar credited with contributions to Hindustani classical music, but not the author of the Natya Shastra.

 

• Tansen (Option 3): A legendary 16th-century classical musician in Emperor Akbar's court, one of the Navaratnas, but not associated with compiling the Natya Shastra.

 

• Kalidas (Option 4): A celebrated Sanskrit poet and playwright (author of works like Abhijnanasakuntalam), not the compiler of the Natya Shastra.

question: In FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022, the opening match was played between Morocco and ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brazil.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2022 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, hosted by India, opened on 11 October 2022 with a Group A match between Morocco and Brazil, played at the Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar, which Brazil won 1–0. (फीफा अंडर-17 महिला विश्व कप 2022 — भारत)

 

• The tournament was hosted across three venues in India: Bhubaneswar, Navi Mumbai, and Goa.

 

• Group A of the tournament comprised India (host nation), USA, Brazil, and Morocco.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Spain won the 2022 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, defeating Colombia in the final.

 

• This was the first FIFA women's tournament to be hosted by India; India had earlier hosted the FIFA U-17 Men's World Cup in 2017.

 

NOTE

 

• India (Option 2): India, the host nation, played in Group A but was not part of the tournament's opening match, which was between Morocco and Brazil.

 

• Chile (Option 3): Chile was not part of Group A and did not play in the opening match of the tournament.

 

• United States of America (Option 4): The USA was in Group A alongside Morocco but did not play in the opening match, which was between Morocco and Brazil.

question: Kailash Satyarthi has received the Noble Prize in the field of _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Peace.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kailash Satyarthi, an Indian child rights and education activist, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014, jointly with Pakistani activist Malala Yousafzai, “for their struggle against the suppression of children and young people and for the right of all children to education.” (कैलाश सत्यार्थी — नोबेल शांति पुरस्कार 2014)

 

• He is the founder of the Bachpan Bachao Andolan (Save the Childhood Movement), an organisation dedicated to rescuing children from bonded labour and trafficking.

 

• He is the second Indian, after Mother Teresa (1979), to receive the Nobel Peace Prize.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kailash Satyarthi has also received other honours, including the Right Livelihood Award and the Harvard Humanitarian Award.

 

• The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway, unlike the other Nobel Prize categories, which are awarded in Stockholm, Sweden.

 

NOTE

 

• Physics (Option 1): Kailash Satyarthi did not receive the Nobel Prize in Physics; this category recognises outstanding contributions to physics research.

 

• Literature (Option 2): He did not receive the Nobel Prize in Literature, which honours outstanding literary work.

 

• Economic studies (Option 4): He did not receive the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences, which recognises contributions to the field of economics.

question: Which of the following statement is NOT correct regarding the prokaryotic cell?
option_1: They have only very small ribosomes as organelles
option_2: Membrane bound cell organelles are present
option_3: Their chromosomes are composed of only nucleic acid.
option_4: Their size is generally in the range of 1 – 10 µm
solution_text:
The correct answer is Membrane bound cell organelles are present.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Prokaryotic cells (such as bacteria) lack a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound cell organelles like mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, and chloroplasts — this is precisely what distinguishes them from eukaryotic cells. Hence, the statement “Membrane bound cell organelles are present” is NOT correct. (प्रोकैरियोटिक कोशिका — कोशिकांगों का अभाव)

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Prokaryotic cells possess only very small ribosomes (70S type) as their sole organelle-like structure; they lack larger membrane-bound organelles.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: The genetic material (chromosome) in prokaryotes is a single, circular, naked DNA molecule, not complexed with histone proteins, and it is composed only of nucleic acid, lying free in the cytoplasm (nucleoid region).

 

• Statement 4 is correct: Prokaryotic cells are generally very small, typically ranging from about 1 to 10 micrometres (µm) in size.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Examples of prokaryotes include bacteria and cyanobacteria (blue-green algae); examples of eukaryotes include plant, animal, fungal, and protist cells.

 

• Eukaryotic cells, by contrast, have a true membrane-bound nucleus along with various membrane-bound organelles and are typically larger (10–100 µm).

 

NOTE

 

• They have only very small ribosomes as organelles (Option 1): This statement is factually correct about prokaryotic cells, so it is not the answer to a “NOT correct” question.

 

• Their chromosomes are composed of only nucleic acid. (Option 3): This statement is factually correct, since prokaryotic DNA is naked (not associated with histones), so it is not the answer.

 

• Their size is generally in the range of 1 – 10 µm (Option 4): This statement is factually correct regarding the typical size range of prokaryotic cells, so it is not the answer.

question: Which of the following statements regarding coal is NOT correct?
option_1: Anthracite is the highest quality hard coal.
option_2: Coal that has been buried deep and subjected to increased temperatures is bituminous coal.
option_3: Lignite is a low-grade brown coal, which is soft with high moisture content.
option_4: Metallurgical coal is high grade lignite coal which has a special value for smelting iron in blast furnaces.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Metallurgical coal is high grade lignite coal which has a special value for smelting iron in blast furnaces.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Metallurgical coal (also called coking coal) is actually a high-grade form of bituminous coal, not lignite coal. It has a special value for smelting iron in blast furnaces because it can be converted into coke, which is used as a reducing agent and fuel in iron and steel production. Hence, calling it “high grade lignite coal” is factually NOT correct. (धात्विक कोयला — बिटुमिनस कोयला, न कि लिग्नाइट)

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Anthracite is indeed the highest quality and hardest form of coal, with the highest carbon content (86–98%) and calorific value among coal types.

 

• Statement 2 is correct: As organic matter is buried deeper and subjected to increasing heat and pressure over geological time (coalification), peat progressively transforms into lignite, then sub-bituminous coal, then bituminous coal, and finally anthracite.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: Lignite is indeed a low-grade, soft, brown coal with a high moisture content and lower carbon content, representing an early stage in coal formation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The coal formation (coalification) series, in order of increasing carbon content and coal rank, is: Peat → Lignite → Sub-bituminous coal → Bituminous coal → Anthracite.

 

• India's major coal reserves are concentrated in states like Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal, and Madhya Pradesh, mostly in the Gondwana coal belts.

 

NOTE

 

• Anthracite is the highest quality hard coal. (Option 1): This statement is factually correct, as anthracite is the highest-grade and hardest coal type, so it is not the answer to a “NOT correct” question.

 

• Coal that has been buried deep and subjected to increased temperatures is bituminous coal. (Option 2): This statement is factually correct regarding the coalification process, so it is not the answer.

 

• Lignite is a low-grade brown coal, which is soft with high moisture content. (Option 3): This statement is factually correct in describing lignite, so it is not the answer.
